translations.text: Peter, apostle of Jesus Christ, to the chosen strangers of the dispersion in Pontus and Galatia, Cappadocia and Bithynia,
by the foreknowledge of God the Father, through the holiness of the Spirit, for obedience and for sprinkling with the blood of Jesus Christ. Grace be with you, and may peace be multiplied!
Blessed is the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who by his great mercy has begotten us again into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,
into an inheritance that is incorruptible, undefiled and unfading, kept in the heavens for you,
who by the power of God are guarded through faith for the salvation that is ready to be revealed at the appointed time.
In this you rejoice, even though for a little while now, if it must be, you have been grieved by many kinds of trials,
so that the testing of your faith, more precious than gold, which perishes and is tested by fire, may be found to result in praise, glory and honour at the revelation of Jesus Christ,
whom you did not know and yet you love, whom you do not see now and yet you believe. Rejoice with a joy that is inexpressible and glorious.
And at the end of your faith you will receive the salvation of souls,
concerning which salvation the prophets who prophesied of the grace meant for you sought and searched,
searching when, or at what time, the Spirit of Christ within them was making it known, when it testified beforehand to the sufferings of Christ and the glories that would follow.

It was revealed to them that they were serving not themselves but you in the things that have now been announced to you by your evangelists through the Holy Spirit sent from heaven, things that angels have longed to see.
Therefore gird up the loins of your minds, be watchful, and hope fully in that grace of theirs [?] that is coming at the revelation of Jesus Christ.
As children of obedience, do not be conformed to the desires you had before, in your ignorance,
but as the one who called you is holy, so you too be holy in all your conduct.
For it is written: Be holy, for I am holy.
And if you call on him as Father who judges each one's work without partiality, live out the time of your sojourning in fear.
Know that you were redeemed from the futile way of life handed down by your fathers not with corruptible silver or gold,
but with the precious blood of Christ, as of an innocent and spotless lamb,
who was foreknown before the creation of the world and was revealed in the last times for your sake;
you who through him are believers in God, who raised him from the dead and gave him glory, so that your faith and hope may be in God.
Purify your souls by obedience to the truth; for the sake of brotherly love be sincere from the heart; love one another earnestly.
For you have been born again, not from corruptible seed but from incorruptible, through the word of God, which is eternal.
For all flesh is grass, and all its glory is like the flower of grass: the grass withered, and its flower fell away.
But the word of the Lord endures forever. This is the word that was preached to you as good news.
Put away all wickedness and all deceit, and hypocrisy, and envy, and every evil word.
Like newborn infants, long for that pure milk, so that by it you may grow into salvation,
since you have tasted that the Lord is sweet.
Come to him, the living stone, who was rejected by people but is chosen and precious in God's sight.
And you too, like living stones, are being built into a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, to offer spiritual sacrifices pleasing to God through Jesus Christ.
For it is written in the scripture: "See, I am laying in Zion a cornerstone, chosen and precious, and whoever believes in him will not be put to shame."

So the honour is for you who believe. But for those who do not believe, "the stone that the builders rejected has become the head of the corner," and "a stone that makes people stumble and a rock that makes them fall."
They stumble at the word because they disobey it, and this is what they were destined for.
But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy seed, a people acquired by God, so that you may proclaim the goodness of the one who called you out of darkness into his marvellous light.
Once you were not God's people, but now you are the people of God. Once you had not been accepted, but now you have received mercy.
Beloved, I urge you, as strangers and passers-by, to keep away from the desires of the flesh, which wage war against the soul.
Live good lives among the Gentiles. Then, although they speak against you as evildoers, they may be put to shame [?] by your good deeds and glorify God on the day of visitation.
For the Lord's sake, submit to every human authority: to the king, because he is over all,
and to governors, because he has sent them to punish those who do evil and to praise those who do good,
to silence the ignorance of foolish people.
Live as free people, but do not use your freedom as a cover for wickedness. Live as servants of God.
Honour everyone, love the brothers, fear God, honour the king.
Servants, submit to your own masters with all fear, not only to those who are good and gentle but also to those who are harsh.
For this is grace from God: if, for the sake of a good conscience, we endure grief and suffer unjustly.
What credit is there if we sin, are beaten for it, and endure it? But if you do good, suffer for it, and endure it, this is grace from God.
This is what you were called to, because Christ also suffered for you and left you a written example, so that you would follow in his footsteps.
He committed no sin, and no deceit was found in his mouth.
When he was insulted, he insulted no one in return. When he suffered, he threatened no one. He was handed over to the judge unjustly.
He himself carried our sins in his body on the tree, so that we might be separated from sin and live by righteousness. By his wounds we have been healed.
You were like sheep that had gone astray, but now you have turned back to the shepherd and guardian of your souls.
Likewise, wives, be subject to your own husbands, so that even if some of them disobey the word, they may be won over without a word by the conduct of their wives,
when they see your holy conduct in fear,
which does not lie in outward braiding of the hair and putting on gold, or in adorning yourselves with clothing,
but in the hidden person of the heart, in the incorruptibility of gentleness and a quiet spirit, which is precious before God.
For in this way the holy women of old, who hoped in God, also adorned themselves and were subject to their own husbands,
as Sarah obeyed Abraham and called him lord. You have become her children if you do good and are not afraid of any fear.
Husbands, likewise, live with them with forbearance, as with the weaker vessel, the female, and give them honour as fellow heirs of the grace of life, so that you do not hinder your prayer.
Finally, all of you be of one mind, merciful, loving the brethren, merciful, humble.
Let none of you repay evil for evil, nor insult for insult; bless the one who opposes you, for to this you were called, that you may inherit a blessing.
For whoever wants the love of life and to see the days of life, let him restrain his tongue from evil and let him not speak deceit with his lips;
let him turn away from evil and do good; let him seek peace and pursue it.
For the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous and his ears are on their prayer; the face of the Lord is against those who do evil.
And who is there to harm you, if you become imitators of what is good?
But even if you suffer for righteousness' sake, you are blessed. Do not be afraid of their fear, and do not be troubled.
Hold the Lord Jesus Christ holy in your hearts. Always be ready to give an answer to everyone who asks you for a word about the hope that is among you, but with gentleness and fear.
Keep a good conscience, so that in the matter in which they speak evil of you, those who oppress you for your good conduct in Christ may be put to shame.
It is better, if the will of God is pleased that you should suffer, to suffer for doing good than for doing evil.
For Christ also suffered once for our sins, the righteous for the false, so that he might bring us to God. He died in the flesh and was made alive in the spirit,
in which he went to the spirits in prison and preached to them,
who were once disobedient, when the long-suffering of God waited patiently in the days of Noah while the ark was being prepared, in which a few, that is, eight souls, were saved from the water.
In the likeness of this, baptism now saves you too: not the removal of filth from the flesh, but the pleasing of God with the mind, through the resurrection of Jesus Christ,
who is at the right hand of God, who ascended into heaven. Angels and authorities and powers were made subject to him.
Since Christ suffered in the flesh, arm yourselves also with the same mind, for whoever has suffered in the flesh has ceased from sin,
so as to live the remaining time in the flesh no longer for human desires, but by the will of God.
The times that have gone by are enough for doing the will of the gentiles, who walk in uncleanness and lust, drunkenness, revelry, feasting, and unseemly idolatry.
Because of this they are astonished that you do not run with them into the same flood of uncleanness, and they blaspheme.
They will give account to him who is ready to judge the living and the dead.
For this is why the dead heard it, so that they might be judged in the flesh as human beings and live through God in the spirit.
The end of all things has come; be pure, be watchful in prayer.
Above all, keep your love for one another fervent, for love covers a multitude of sins.
Be hospitable to one another without grumbling.
Each of you, as you have received grace from God, use it in the same way to serve one another, as good stewards of the manifold gift of God.

Whoever speaks, let him speak with the word of God. Whoever serves, let him serve as from the strength that God gives, so that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom belong glory and power forever. Amen.
Beloved, do not be astonished at the fiery ordeal among you, which comes upon you as a trial, as though something strange were happening to you.
But insofar as you share in the sufferings of Christ, rejoice, so that at the revelation of his glory you may also rejoice and be glad.
If you are reproached for the name of the Lord, you are blessed, for the Spirit of glory, the Spirit of God, rests upon you.
Let none of you suffer as a murderer, or a thief, or an evildoer, or as one who meddles in the affairs of others;
but if one suffers as a Christian, let him not be ashamed, but let him glorify God by that name.
For the time of judgment begins first with the house of God; and if it begins first with us, what will be the end of those who disobey the gospel of God?
And if the righteous is saved with difficulty, where will the ungodly and the sinner appear?
Therefore let those who suffer according to the will of God entrust their souls to the faithful Creator by doing good.
I exhort the elders among you, as a fellow elder and a witness of the sufferings of Christ, and a sharer in the glory that is to be revealed: shepherd the flock of God that is among you,
taking care of it not under compulsion but willingly, as God wills; not for shameful gain, but eagerly;
not as lording it over the priests, but becoming an example to the flock.
And when the chief shepherd appears, you will receive the unfading crown of glory.
Likewise, you who are younger, submit to the elders; and all of you clothe yourselves with humility toward one another, for God crushes the proud but gives grace to the humble.
Humble yourselves, therefore, under the mighty hand of God, so that he may exalt you at the time of his visitation.
Cast all your care on him, for he takes care of you.
Be on guard, keep awake, for your adversary the devil walks about like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour.
Resist him firmly in the faith, knowing that the same sufferings [?] are being fulfilled in your brotherhood in this world.
But may the God of all grace, who called you to his eternal glory through Christ Jesus, after you have suffered a little, himself strengthen you and establish you,
for his is the might forever and ever. Amen.
Through Silvanus, your faithful brother, as I consider him, I have written to you briefly, exhorting you and testifying that this is the true grace in which you stand.
She who is in Babylon, chosen together with you, greets you, and so does Mark, my son.
Greet one another with a kiss of love. Peace be with you, all who are in Christ Jesus.
